name: Namibia

findings.summary: Telecom Namibia announced a five-year partnership to buy Huawei mobile radio access equipment, adding and upgrading base stations for 4G, 4.5G and 5G coverage, including underserved rural areas, under its strategic plan to 2027.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 3 on a stated equipment-purchase partnership; value and site count not disclosed, and no formal contract document seen. Core network not covered by this release (see NAM-002). The Brief largely relays the operator's release, so independence is limited.

findings.summary: Telecom Namibia signed a deal reported at US$5.3 million with Huawei for a fixed-mobile convergence core network; it began 5G testing with Huawei in March 2024 and targets commercial 5G in 2026.
findings.analyst_inference: Signing year 2023 inferred from the article's 'last year' wording (article dated 2024-08-28). Value as reported in USD; no award notice seen.

findings.summary: MTC, Namibia's largest mobile operator, launched commercial 5G in Windhoek, Walvis Bay, Swakopmund and Ongwediva, with Huawei named as a 5G partner under an agreement signed the previous year.
findings.analyst_inference: Huawei is named as one 5G partner, not confirmed as sole RAN/core vendor; tier 3 for the signed agreement rather than tier 5, since launch covers four towns. Commercial launch implies Namibia's earlier 5G moratorium (reasons unstated in sources) was lifted. A 2022 MTC-Huawei-NUST cooperation agreement and Global Voices' description of Huawei as long-time 3G/4G supplier to MTC and Telecom Namibia were seen but not coded separately.

findings.controller: Government of Namibia (Ministry of Information and Communication Technology)
findings.local_actor: Ministry of Information and Communication Technology; Office of the Prime Minister
findings.summary: Namibia plans a national data centre under its 2025-2029 digital strategy; the ICT ministry and Prime Minister's office are finalising a concept note, with capacity, builder, financier and cost not yet disclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 1: planning statement only. Domestic on the assumption the state will own and operate it; no builder, financier or equipment vendor named, so a foreign controller cannot be ruled out.

findings.local_actor: City of Windhoek; Mobile Telecommunications Company (MTC)
findings.summary: MTC donated about 200 CCTV cameras to the City of Windhoek, to be installed on MTC infrastructure and at more than 40 crime-prone sites including the central business district.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: camera vendor not stated. Tier 3 for a completed donation; installation not confirmed. Scale municipal (one city). Whether the cameras are Huawei/Hikvision/Dahua or other was not established.

silicon.null_reason: no accelerator purchases surfaced in facilities or AI searches; no dedicated silicon search given budget

models.null_reason: one search found only a Deloitte AI-strategy advisory engagement (Aug 2026) and a national AI institute; no model-provider partnership or national model

research_gaps: Who imposed Namibia's 5G moratorium (c. 2020-2022), on what grounds (environmental, security, Huawei?), and when was it formally lifted?
Is Huawei MTC's sole 5G RAN/core vendor, and which vendor supplies MTC's legacy 3G/4G network (S1/S2 confirmation)?
Vendor of the ~200 CCTV cameras MTC donated to the City of Windhoek, and of other city/police CCTV (City of Windhoek-PowerCom MoU; earlier N$25m city cameras).
Owner and status of Paratus Armada data centre (Windhoek) and any post-2023 AI/large data-centre projects; national data centre builder and financier.
Submarine cable landings (WACS, Equiano) and any HMN Tech involvement in Namibian cable projects.
